narrationTexts: I'll start by looking at the project.
3 real failures, all in `orderTotal`. Let me look at the code.
The doc comment says tax goes on the discounted amount, but the code taxes the pre-discount base. One-line fix:
finalText:
Green: 625/625 passing.

**What was broken:** only 3 of the 625 cases actually failed, all in `orderTotal` (`src/pricing.js:40`). The rest of the wall of text was passing-case noise.

The function applied the discount, then computed tax on the *original* `cents` instead of the discounted amount — contradicting its own docstring ("Tax is charged on the amount the customer pays"). So every order with both a nonzero discount and nonzero tax rate was overcharged by `discount × taxRate`. The 66 passing cases in that suite all had either 0% off or 0 tax, which is why it slipped through.

```js
const tax = roundCents(discounted * taxRate);  // was: cents * taxRate
```

Worth noting this was a live overcharge bug, not just a test discrepancy — e.g. a 33400c order at 10% off with 20% tax was billing 36740 instead of 36072.
